)

blocks.text: Together, the two models achieve SOTA on all six Chinese and English single-tag metrics; tiny also leads all three English multi-tag metrics. Chinese multi-tag control remains behind NV-CV3.

blocks.text: Tiny is stronger in Sichuanese control accuracy and achieves SOTA Sichuanese Hard CER and Easy ACC, while 0.5b achieves SOTA Cantonese Base CER and ACC. Cantonese speaker similarity remains below CosyVoice2-Yue. Historical Ming-omni-tts results remain stronger on Sichuanese Easy CER (2.25%), Hard SIM (0.750) and Hard ACC (90.45%), and on Cantonese Coverage CER (7.87%).

Tiny ranks third on German SIM (0.791), but neither model reaches the top three in the other four new languages. French SIM is 0.675 for 0.5b and 0.733 for tiny; both also trail CosyVoice2-Yue on Cantonese SIM.
; stability with many tags per sentence is still improving.
When the words carry no emotional signal (CV3-Eval Text-Unrelated, and most of the hard set), accuracy drops well below the Text-Related half.
Pitch is the least accurate attribute for both models. Tiny's 78.70% ranks 2nd, 7.30 percentage points below 0.5b's 86.00%; the historical Ming-omni-tts-0.5B score is 91.33%.
RP is the lowest voice design sub-score, ranking 4th for tiny (61.10%) and 5th for 0.5b (61.06%).
Tiny's Korean CER (6.000%) ranks 6th, well behind 0.5b's 1.728% (3rd).
Tiny's UTMOS of 2.12 ranks 2nd, below ZipVoice-Dia's 2.24 and the historical Ming-omni-tts-0.5B score of 2.25.
